key_insight: iPANNs and fPANNs learn physics-constrained lower/mean/upper hyperelastic energy bounds that quantify uncertainty while keeping predicted stresses consistent with noisy data.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact, distribution-free way to build constitutive models that are more reliable for finite element analysis when experimental stress-deformation data are sparse or noisy.
method: Train a sparse mean free-energy network first, then fine-tune lower and upper branches via transfer learning.
Use automatic differentiation to convert learned energy branches into stress bounds that enclose observations.
Extend interval bounds to fuzzy uncertainty with alpha-cut interpolation, while enforcing objectivity, consistency, and polyconvexity.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates synthetic isotropic hyperelastic datasets with heteroscedastic noise, varying random realizations, shifted noise means, and different noise magnitudes, and reports that the learned bounds enclose noisy stress observations and generalize to test data.
watch_item: The approach adds model and training complexity, and performance may depend on the quality of sparse data and the stability of the two-stage regularized optimization.
paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
